title: Understanding Saving Behavior: An Investigation of Factors Influencing Filipino University Students' Saving Habits
authors: Claros, J.; Fernandez, P.; Rodriguez, A.
venue: Mindanao State University — Iligan Institute of Technology Research Journal
tldr: University allowance amount is the primary predictor of monthly savings, followed by peer saving norms and self-discipline. Parents' education and employment status also significantly influence saving behavior.
problem_and_motivation: Filipino university students face financial challenges exacerbated by economic disruptions, yet limited research examines the specific factors influencing their saving behavior. Understanding these factors is essential for developing financial education programs that improve students' financial resilience.
approach: Conducted cross-sectional survey of 271 university students from three campuses (University of the Philippines, Polytechnic University of the Philippines, and Far Eastern University) using stratified random sampling.
Developed a 42-item questionnaire measuring six constructs: peer influence, parental influence, self-discipline, financial habits, financial knowledge, and allowance amount.
Applied descriptive statistics, correlation analysis (Pearson r), and multiple linear regression to identify predictors.
Used Likert scale responses (1=Strongly Disagree to 5=Strongly Agree) across all behavioral items.
Tested five hypotheses about relationships between demographic/behavioral factors and monthly savings.
findings: University allowance amount is the strongest positive predictor of monthly savings (r = 0.68, p < 0.05).
Students with allowance above PHP 10,000 save an average of PHP 3,800 monthly compared to PHP 1,200 for those with allowance below PHP 5,000.
Peer saving norms are the strongest behavioral predictor (β = 0.314, p < 0.05), with peers' savings behavior positively correlating with individual savings.
Self-discipline has the highest regression coefficient (β = 0.352), indicating it is the strongest behavioral predictor of monthly savings.
Parents' education level significantly influences saving behavior: children of college-educated parents save 45% more monthly.
Parents' employment status shows a significant relationship with students' savings (r = 0.32, p < 0.05).
54% of students reported saving PHP 1,000–3,000 monthly, while only 23% save above PHP 3,000.
68% of students use cash-based budgeting, while only 32% use digital financial tools.
Students with part-time jobs save 35% more than those without.

topics.name: Income and Cash-Flow Pattern Classification
topics.justification: Directly examines income (allowance) as a predictor of saving behavior, classifying students by allowance brackets and analyzing cash-flow patterns through monthly savings.

topics.name: Peer Norms and Social Comparison Mechanics
topics.justification: Studies peer saving norms as a behavioral predictor, finding that friends' saving behavior positively correlates with individual savings through social comparison mechanisms.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper identifies the key predictors of Filipino university students' saving behavior, establishing that allowance amount is the strongest financial predictor while self-discipline and peer norms are the strongest behavioral predictors. It provides empirical evidence for the role of parental influence and socioeconomic background in shaping saving habits, informing the design of financial education interventions targeting youth.
directly_justifies: Allowance amount is the strongest financial predictor of monthly savings (r = 0.68).
Peer saving norms positively influence individual savings through social comparison.
Self-discipline (β = 0.352) is the strongest behavioral predictor of saving behavior.
Parents' education and employment status significantly influence students' financial habits.
Students with part-time jobs save 35% more than those without.
limits: Cross-sectional design limits causal inference about the direction of peer influence.
Self-reported saving amounts may be subject to recall bias and social desirability bias.
Three-campus sample may not represent the broader Filipino university student population.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: A systematic scan of all topic domains was conducted. Domain 1 (Income Classification & Cash-Flow) was selected because the paper directly analyzes allowance (income) as a predictor of saving behavior and classifies students by income brackets. Domain 4 (Spending Drivers & Behavioral Finance) was selected because the paper examines peer norms and social comparison as behavioral drivers of financial decisions. No other domains from the taxonomy match the paper's focus.

limitations: Limited to three Metro Manila universities, potentially not representative of rural or provincial students.
Cross-sectional design prevents establishing causal relationships between variables.
Reliance on self-reported data introduces potential measurement bias.
remember_this: University allowance amount is the strongest predictor of monthly savings (r = 0.68).
Self-discipline (β = 0.352) outperforms peer norms (β = 0.314) as a behavioral predictor.
Students with allowance above PHP 10,000 save PHP 3,800 monthly versus PHP 1,200 for those below PHP 5,000.
Parents' education level increases monthly savings by 45% for their children.
68% of students still use cash-based budgeting rather than digital tools.
